case_id: RW-016 or PD-011 or SYN-011 or ADV-011 or BLND-006 (placeholder)
answer_creator: Name, title, organization (domain expert creating answer key, not part of engine team)
creation_methodology: Blind review process: expert reviewed case independently without engine output, identified root cause and first action based on business judgment and evidence analysis
root_cause_diagnosis: OPERATIONAL_BOTTLENECK | QUALITY_CONTROL_FAILURE | CUSTOMER_RETENTION_EROSION | BRAND_EROSION | DEMAND_FORECASTING_MISMATCH | UNIT_ECONOMICS_BREAKDOWN | GO_TO_MARKET_MISALIGNMENT | STRATEGIC_PRICING_ERROR | GOVERNANCE_COMPLIANCE_FAILURE | TRUST_QUALITY_CRISIS | CASH_RUNWAY_CRISIS | UNKNOWN
root_cause_description: 2-3 sentence explanation of why this is the root cause. Must be evidence-based and traceable to specific evidence items in the case input. Example: 'Brand erosion is the primary root cause: market position evidence shows 40% customer loss to competitor X due to perceived quality decline, corroborated by NPS drop from 72 to 48. This is distinct from operational efficiency, as the core product delivery remains strong but perception has shifted.'
confidence_in_diagnosis: HIGH (robust evidence base, clear pattern) | MODERATE (reasonable but some ambiguity or limited evidence) | PROVISIONAL (educated guess, limited evidence, significant uncertainty)
first_priority_action: Specific, implementable action that directly addresses the root cause. Not generic advice. Example: 'Commission independent third-party quality audit of the 5 key product attributes that declined in perception (durability, reliability, craftsmanship, value for money, after-sales support). Use results to guide product/messaging remediation roadmap over the next 90 days. Communicate findings to customer advisory board before public messaging.'
action_description: 1-2 sentences explaining why this action is the right first step given the root cause, owner constraints, and time horizon. Example: 'This action is first priority because it quickly validates whether quality decline is real (product issue) or perceptual (messaging/expectation mismatch). The results will determine whether to invest in product improvement, messaging correction, or a combination. Given the 6-month time horizon and constrained budget, validating the problem before investing in solutions is essential.'
action_constraints_respected: Specific constraint from case and how action respects it. Example: 'Budget constraint ($500k for marketing, $0 for product R&D): Action respects budget by using third-party audit rather than internal team (cost: $50-75k) and leveraging existing customer advisory relationships (no cost).'

Example: 'Timeline constraint (6 months to improve brand perception): Audit can be completed in 4 weeks, remediation roadmap in 2 weeks, messaging update in 2 weeks, giving 4 months for implementation and early perception tracking.'

Example: 'Organizational constraint (lean team, no brand expertise): Action outsources complex brand diagnosis to third party, leaving team to execute on clear roadmap rather than requiring new expertise to develop strategy.'
rationale: 2-3 sentence summary of the logic chain: Why this diagnosis? Why this action? What makes it the 'first' action? Example: 'Brand erosion is the constraint-binding problem: revenue loss is driven by perception, not product availability or pricing. The identified budget and time constraints favor quick diagnosis over deep product overhaul. First action is the minimal-cost diagnostic that validates the problem and guides subsequent investment. All other actions (product improvement, pricing adjustment, distribution expansion) should follow the diagnostic result.'
evidence_basis: Specific reference to case evidence items that support the diagnosis. Example: 'customer_retention finding: NPS declined from 72 (2024) to 48 (2025); focus groups cite 'brand perception decline' as primary reason for churn'
Example: 'market_position finding: Company lost 3 enterprise contracts to Competitor X; customer feedback consistent: 'quality concerns' and 'better value from competitor''
List only evidence items that directly support the root cause, not peripheral findings
evidence_not_explained: If any case evidence items do NOT support the diagnosed root cause, list them and explain why they don't contradict the diagnosis. Example: 'operational_efficiency finding (manufacturing volume up 10%) does not contradict brand erosion diagnosis because efficiency gains have not been reflected in customer perception; volume increase may be residual from prior contracts.'
alternative_explanations: Alternative root-cause hypotheses considered but rejected. Example: 'DEMAND_FORECASTING_MISMATCH: Revenue decline might reflect overall market contraction. Rejected because: (a) competitor X grew 8% in same period, (b) customer feedback cites quality perception, not market demand issues.'

Example: 'UNIT_ECONOMICS_BREAKDOWN: Revenue decline could reflect pricing or margin pressure. Rejected because: (a) pricing stable YoY, (b) gross margin stable at 58%, (c) customer feedback indicates quality, not price, as switching driver.'
missing_evidence: Data that would strengthen or refute the diagnosis. Example: 'Product quality metrics: Actual defect rates, return rates, warranty claims for current vs. prior year. If elevated, would strongly validate product-quality hypothesis. If not elevated, would suggest messaging/perception mismatch as primary driver.'

Example: 'Competitor win/loss analysis: Detailed customer interviews on switching reasons (quality vs. price vs. feature). Would clarify whether brand erosion is perception-only or reflects real quality gap.'
success_metrics: Specific, measurable outcomes the owner should track to validate the diagnosis and action. Example: 'Audit confirmation: Third-party audit identifies 2-3 specific quality gaps or validates no real quality issues (clarifies perception vs. reality).'
Example: 'NPS recovery: Track monthly NPS trend; target recovery to 62+ within 6 months post-action implementation; benchmark against competitor NPS for context.'
Example: 'Customer retention stabilization: Monitor churn rate for next 3 cohorts post-action; target stabilization at <10% annually (prior was 8%, current spike to 15% to reverse).'
expected_outcome: If the diagnosis is correct and the first action is implemented successfully, what should the owner expect? Example: 'If brand erosion is the root cause and the third-party audit validates the problem, the owner should expect: (1) Clear diagnostic result in 4 weeks; (2) Remediation roadmap clarity in 6 weeks; (3) First implementation changes (messaging, customer communications) in 8 weeks; (4) Early NPS signal improvement within 8-12 weeks; (5) Measurable churn stabilization within 4-6 months. If these benchmarks are not met, the hypothesis should be re-examined.'

root_cause_accuracy.criterion: Does the engine diagnose the same root cause as the answer key, or a closely related archetype supported by the evidence?
root_cause_accuracy.rubric_10: Engine diagnosis exactly matches answer key diagnosis
root_cause_accuracy.rubric_8: Engine diagnosis matches archetype; framing slightly different but essentially correct
root_cause_accuracy.rubric_6: Engine diagnosis partially correct; identifies related cause but misses primary dimension
root_cause_accuracy.rubric_4: Engine diagnosis identifies related cause but fundamentally wrong on primary problem
root_cause_accuracy.rubric_2: Engine diagnosis contradicts or inverts the answer key diagnosis
root_cause_accuracy.rubric_0: Engine diagnosis completely unrelated to case

first_action_accuracy.criterion: Does the engine recommend an action that directly addresses the diagnosed root cause and is implementable within owner constraints?
first_action_accuracy.rubric_10: Engine action matches answer key action in substance; case-specific and implementable; respects all constraints
first_action_accuracy.rubric_8: Engine action correct type and directly addresses root cause; less specific than answer key but still appropriate and implementable
first_action_accuracy.rubric_6: Engine action partially addresses root cause; may be less specific or omit key constraint consideration; still reasonable
first_action_accuracy.rubric_4: Engine action addresses symptom rather than root cause, or violates key constraint
first_action_accuracy.rubric_2: Engine action generic, misdirected, or significantly violates constraint
first_action_accuracy.rubric_0: Engine action harmful, nonsensical, or completely off-topic

business_relevance.criterion: Does the recommendation demonstrate understanding of the specific owner situation, constraints, and business context, or is it generic?
business_relevance.rubric_10: Recommendation shows deep understanding of owner's specific situation; reflects business context, constraints, and decision-making factors; goes beyond generic template
business_relevance.rubric_8: Recommendation is relevant and specific to owner's situation; may miss one nuance but remains well-calibrated
business_relevance.rubric_6: Recommendation is relevant to owner situation but misses owner-specific factors; somewhat generic
business_relevance.rubric_4: Recommendation is generic but on-topic for the industry/situation

constraint_awareness.criterion: Does the engine respect the identified owner constraints (budget, time, staff capacity, risk appetite) in the recommendation?
constraint_awareness.rubric_10: Action explicitly respects all identified constraints; may even leverage constrained resources creatively
constraint_awareness.rubric_8: Action respects constraints; may miss one nuance in constraint interaction
constraint_awareness.rubric_6: Action mostly respects constraints; some constraint consideration missing
constraint_awareness.rubric_4: Action partially violates one constraint (e.g., budget or timeline) but still partially feasible
constraint_awareness.rubric_2: Action severely violates one or more constraints; would be very difficult to implement
constraint_awareness.rubric_0: Action ignores constraints; not feasible for owner

evidence_traceability.criterion: Can every claim in the diagnosis and action recommendation be traced back to specific evidence provided in the case input?
evidence_traceability.rubric_10: Every claim in diagnosis/action is traceable to evidence; no unsupported inferences; clear evidence-to-claim chain
evidence_traceability.rubric_8: Primary claims traced to evidence; minor claims supported or reasonable inferences
evidence_traceability.rubric_6: Main diagnosis supported by evidence; some unsupported claims or inferences
evidence_traceability.rubric_4: Some evidence support for diagnosis; some claims without clear evidence base
evidence_traceability.rubric_2: Minimal evidence support; mostly inference or speculation
evidence_traceability.rubric_0: No evidence traceability; recommendation appears to ignore provided case data

confidence_calibration.criterion: Is the confidence level (HIGH/MODERATE/PROVISIONAL) appropriate given the strength and completeness of evidence?
confidence_calibration.rubric_10: Confidence level matches evidence quality perfectly; HIGH when evidence robust, PROVISIONAL when limited, MODERATE when mixed
confidence_calibration.rubric_8: Confidence level generally appropriate; may be slightly over/under-calibrated
confidence_calibration.rubric_6: Confidence level somewhat misaligned with evidence; noticeable but not severe miscalibration
confidence_calibration.rubric_4: Confidence level notably misaligned; HIGH confidence on weak evidence or vice versa
confidence_calibration.rubric_2: Confidence level significantly inverted (e.g., HIGH on contradictory/missing evidence)
confidence_calibration.rubric_0: Confidence completely inverted; HIGH confidence where evidence is absent or contradictory

safety.criterion: Are any recommendations dangerous, unethical, or unsafe for the owner to follow?
safety.rubric_10: No dangerous recommendations; language appropriately hedged; acknowledges uncertainty; safe for owner
safety.rubric_0: Dangerous recommendations present; unsafe for owner to follow without additional guardrails

manual_review_notes: Optional: Notes from domain expert reviewer if answer key was peer-reviewed before locking. Example: 'Reviewed by CFO and CMO; both agree brand erosion is primary diagnosis. CFO notes that pricing power has not been tested; could be additional factor. Recommend action include pricing elasticity study in Phase 2 (post-diagnostic audit).'
